svg.title: All 56 tools are native — but only 23 ship first
svg.desc: Breakdown of the one IDE surface, Copilot in VS Code, which enabled 56 tools at the baseline. All 56 are native to VS Code; there is no MCP server or third-party tool surface in this run. The harness sends only 23 full schemas on the first request (about 9,200 tokens) and defers the other 33, which carry a defer_loading flag and load on demand when the model calls the built-in tool_search tool. The system block also folds in 16 skill blocks and an 8-agent roster, but those are mostly not product defaults: 9 come straight from the workspace repository's .github folder, 8 from user-installed extensions, and only 6 are Copilot built-ins. Git branch and status and workspace metadata are workspace-derived. The export does not expose a clean system-versus-context wire split, so finer attribution is not observable.
svg.text: An IDE adds a workspace, not just a window
Copilot in VS Code, baseline: 56 native tools split by how they are delivered.
56 native tools — 23 sent on first request + 33 deferred (loaded via tool_search)
23 active schemas are ~9,200 tok; the full catalog would be ~16,600 tok if sent flat. Deferral keeps ~7,000 tok out of the first request.
Tool schemas sent on first call (23) — Native — core file/search/terminal/edit/planning + tool_search
Tool schemas deferred (33) — Native — load on demand via tool_search (defer_loading: true)
System instructions + 16 skills / 8 agents — Mostly repo .github + installed extensions — folded into system block
Git branch / status, workspace metadata — Workspace-derived
System-vs-context wire split — Not observable from the export
Source: co-ide-exports/CO-IDE_agent_sonnet_MCPoff.json. All 56 tools native (no MCP); 23/33 split read from per-tool defer_loading flags. System + skills + context folded into one block.
